background.text: uh nine years being the mayor obviously there are an enormous amount of things that you could have not have predicted on pandemics etc but walking into the job has it have there been things that you expected and have there been did it live up to your expectations

ground_truth: You know, I'm one of these people who's superstitious and never guesses what it's gonna be like. Cause I always experience in life, whatever you think something's gonna be like, it's gonna surprise you and maybe be the opposite. So when I was running for office, I never pictured it. I kind of waited till I was here on day one. Obviously the building was familiar. 12 years I had served as a local public servant, but coming downstairs from the fourth floor where the city council offices are to the third floor here was almost like going into a different world. Going from the legislative branch to the executive branch, it never ceased and ceases to amaze me just how different the job is and how exciting it is. I used to think the city council, oh my gosh, I had so much power, I could write legislation. And it's true, the city council jobs are immensely powerful. You can impact your district in profound ways and pass legislation for the city. But as the chief executive of the city, there is probably a hundred decisions a week that equal the number of big decisions I'd make in a year as a council member. So you have to be ready to run numerous departments. You have to be comfortable being an executive. This was my first executive position and I loved being an executive because the speed with which you can act is just so different. The way you can set a vision and explain a moment. Those things to me really were totally different than anything I had done and were not only a surprise, but a pleasant surprise, I'd say 90% of the time.
